import os,glob,re
def load():

        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))

def find_lines(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    from collections import Counter
    bg=Counter(x for r in g for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    px={(r,c,g[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if g[r][c]!=bg}
    bottom=max(r for r,c,v in px)
    anchors={c:v for r,c,v in px if r==bottom}
    assert len(anchors)==2, anchors
    lines=[]
    for c0,v in anchors.items():
        for d in (1,-1):
            # candidate line: col = c0 + d*(bottom-r); valid if all other px of color v... just take the one passing through most object pixels
            cells={(r,c0+d*(bottom-r)) for r in range(h) if 0<=c0+d*(bottom-r)<w}
            lines.append((sum(1 for r,c,vv in px if (r,c) in cells and vv==v),d,c0,v,cells))
    lines.sort(reverse=True)
    taken=set()
    out=[[bg]*w for _ in range(h)]
    for n,d,c0,v,cells in lines[:2]:
        if (d,c0,v) in taken: continue
        taken.add((d,c0,v))
        for r,c in cells: out[r][c]=v
    return out
